title: Enterprise onboarding, integration, QBR & escalation playbook
author: Marina Alvarez
body:
Overview

This playbook consolidates the standard enterprise onboarding sequence, integration checklist, escalation procedures, known issues & mitigations, and Health/QBR templates used by Redwood Inference Customer Success and Support teams. It is intended for CSMs, Solutions Engineers (SEs), Support Engineers, and SREs who run or support enterprise onboarding programs.

Scope

- Applies to all new Dedicated and Private customers, and to self-serve customers moving to sales-assisted plans.
- Covers technical onboarding (integration & testing), operational readiness (SLOs, monitoring), escalation paths, and recurring health/QBR cadence.

Goals

1. Accelerate time-to-first-successful-inference (target: <14 days for standard integrations).
2. Ensure production readiness with agreed SLOs and runbooks.
3. Reduce escalations by capturing common failure modes and mitigations.
4. Provide consistent QBR artifacts to demonstrate value and surface opportunities.

Roles and responsibilities

- Customer Success Manager (CSM): owns customer relationship, business objectives, QBRs, and cross-functional coordination.
- Solutions Engineer (SE): owns technical onboarding, integration validation, and knowledge transfer.
- Support Engineer (L2): owns post-go-live operational issues and triage.
- SRE/Infra: supports capacity, network, and production runbooks (on-call for Dedicated/Private).
- Customer Technical Lead: owns customer-side changes, proxy/network configuration, and test data.

Pre-onboarding checklist (items to complete before kickoff)

| Item | Owner | Required by kickoff? | Notes |
|------|-------|---------------------|-------|
| Signed contract & billing setup | Sales/Finance | Yes | Order number and region must be confirmed. |
| Technical contacts & escalation matrix | CSM | Yes | Names, emails, and PagerDuty IDs. |
| Network allowlist (if Private) | Customer/SE | Yes | See network requirements table below. |
| Test dataset & sample prompts | Customer/SE | Yes | Include edge cases and privacy-sensitive examples. |
| Model/version & throughput targets | CSM/SE | Yes | Define expected QPS and P95 latency targets. |

Network & environment requirements (summary)

- For Hosted/Dedicated: outbound TLS (443) to api.redwood.ai endpoints; optional VPC peering for Dedicated.
- For Private: VPN or VPC configuration; customer must provide dedicated subnets and NAT/Gateway.

Sample network config table:

| Component | Ports | Protocol | Notes |
|----------|-------|----------|-------|
| API endpoint (host) | 443 | TLS | Customer needs egress to api.redwood.<region>.internal |
| Metrics/Tracing endpoint | 443, 8125 | TLS, UDP | Optional - for extended observability |
| SFTP (optional) | 22 | SSH | For batch data ingestion, use scoped accounts |

Onboarding timeline (90-day recommended sequence)

Days 0-7: Kickoff and discovery
1. Kickoff meeting (CSM, SE, Customer TL) - agree success criteria and timeline.
2. Finalize access and contacts.
3. Baseline acceptance tests: 10 end-to-end sample requests.

Days 8-21: Integration & validation
1. Network validation and allowlist confirmation.
2. API key provisioning and role-based tokens.
3. Initial performance run (synthetic load) to validate P95 latency and concurrency targets.
4. Data-handling review if customer sends PII.

Days 22-45: Pilot & quality validation
1. Pilot with real traffic (shadow or low % of production).
2. Capture quality metrics (e.g., NPS-like survey for outputs, task-specific metrics).
3. Iterate on prompts, model variant selection, and quantization profiles.

Days 46-90: Go-live & stabilization
1. Ramp plan to full traffic (staged % increases).
2. Define SLOs and error budgets; set alert thresholds.
3. Schedule QBR cadence and handoff to support/ops.

Integration guide (core steps and common commands)

1) API access and auth
- Provision API tokens scoped to the customer environment.
- For Dedicated/Private, follow the \"service account\" creation checklist in eng-platform/runbooks.
- Example curl (replace <KEY> and <ENDPOINT>):
  curl -s -H \"Authorization: Bearer <KEY>\" \"https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate\" -d '{\"input\":\"Hello\"}'

2) Prompts and rate limiting
- Default rate limits for Dedicated: configured per contract (typically 100-2,000 RPS depending on pool size).
- Recommend client-side retries with exponential backoff: 500ms base, 2 retries.

3) Observability & logs
- Enable request-level tracing headers (X-Request-ID).
- Hook to metrics endpoint for: token_count, latency_ms_p50/p95, error_rate.

4) Security & data flows
- For Private: ensure KMS/HSM integration for key wrapping.
- For Hosted: custom data classification tags can be used to opt-out of retention.

Escalation playbook (severity, routing, and actions)

Severity definitions
- Sev 1 (Critical): Production outage making the service unusable for all users (e.g., model serving down, auth outage). Target response: 15 minutes.
- Sev 2 (High): Degraded production impacting a substantial portion of traffic (e.g., sustained high error rate, elevated latency above SLO). Target response: 1 hour.
- Sev 3 (Medium): Functional issues affecting a subset of features or customers with workarounds (e.g., degraded performance for large sequences). Target response: 1 business day.
- Sev 4 (Low): Cosmetic or operational requests, feature questions, or non-urgent configuration changes. Target response: 3 business days.

Escalation steps (for Sev 1-2)
1. Triage (Support Engineer on duty): gather logs, request IDs, customer-impact scope, and a short impact statement.
2. Notify CSM and SE; open an incident in our incident tracker and link to PagerDuty incident.
3. If infrastructure (GPU pool, network, auth) is implicated, page SRE and Runtime on-call.
4. Provide customer-facing interim status updates every 30 minutes for Sev 1, hourly for Sev 2 until resolved.
5. Post-incident: create postmortem within 72 hours if Sev 1, 5 business days for Sev 2.

Escalation contacts (summary)

| Role | Primary contact | PagerDuty | Notes |
|------|-----------------|----------|-------|
| Support L2 | support-team@redwood.ai | PD_SUPPORT | 24/7 queue for customer-facing incidents |
| Runtime on-call | runtime-oncall@redwood.ai | PD_RUNTIME | Handles model-serving and kernel issues |
| SRE infra | sre-oncall@redwood.ai | PD_SRE | Network, capacity, and cloud incidents |

Known issues and workarounds (selected items)

1) Symptom: P95 latency spikes when sequence length increases unexpectedly.
- Cause: batching and KV cache eviction under longer sequences.
- Workaround: configure per-request max_sequence_length and enable prefix caching for stable chat sessions.
- Permanent fix: schedule model variant with larger KV allocation or adjust batching policy.

2) Symptom: Intermittent 401 errors during token rotation.
- Cause: Token rolling script timing mismatch.
- Workaround: retry with exponential backoff; confirm clock sync on customer side and server.
- Permanent fix: update token rotation orchestration to pre-warm new tokens 60s before expiry.

3) Symptom: Embeddings mismatch for similar inputs after a model upgrade.
- Cause: upstream model change or quantization variant change.
- Workaround: pin to previous model version for critical flows and run regression evals.
- Permanent fix: introduce automated pre-rollout evals against customer prompt-set and automatic canary traffic gating.

4) Symptom: High error rate for Private deploys after network policy change.
- Cause: Firewall rules blocking health-check or metrics endpoints.
- Workaround: instruct customer to allowlist internal health endpoints and re-run health checks.

Support process & runbook links

- L1 triage (CSM/Support): reproduce, collect sample request IDs, identify scope.
- L2 handling: deep-dive logs, engage SE or Runtime depending on root cause.
- Incident review & follow-up: schedule remediation work and roll into product backlog if needed.

Suggested runbook links (internal)
- eng-servic e/runtime-architecture/runbooks/serving-down
- eng-sre/runbooks/capacity-degradation
- security-and-compliance/incident-response-security

Health checks and QBR materials

Operational metrics to monitor (minimum):
- Request success rate (1 - 5xx) - target >= 99.5%
- Token throughput (tokens/sec) - compare to contract forecast
- Latency P50/P95/P99 (ms) - ensure within contracted SLOs
- Cost per 1K tokens (USD) - track efficiency improvements
- Model quality: task-specific metric (e.g., accuracy, ROUGE, human rating)

Weekly health check template (CSM & SE)
- Customer: <name>
- Week of: <date range>
- Summary: short narrative (1-2 lines)
- Key metrics: success rate, p95 latency, error spikes (include timestamps)
- Open action items: owner, due date
- Risks: list items that could impact go-live or SLOs

Quarterly QBR agenda (suggested)
1. Business goals review (CSM) - align on objectives and KPIs.
2. Usage & economics (Finance/CSM) - usage trends, cost per request, forecast.
3. Reliability & incidents (SRE/Support) - SLO adherence, recent incidents, remediation.
4. Quality & model roadmap (SE/Product) - output quality, regression alerts, upcoming model changes.
5. Roadmap & next steps (Customer + Redwood) - prioritized initiatives and owners.

QBR deliverables
- Executive one-pager (1 page): current state, top 3 wins, top 3 risks.
- Appendix: Metric dashboards, recent incident summaries, action-tracker.

Template queries (example)
- Error rate by endpoint (last 30d): SELECT endpoint, sum(errors)/sum(requests) AS error_rate FROM metrics WHERE customer_id='CUSTOMER_ID' GROUP BY endpoint;
- Latency p95 (last 7d): SELECT percentile(latency_ms, 95) FROM requests WHERE customer_id='CUSTOMER_ID' AND timestamp > now() - interval '7 days';

Onboarding sign-off checklist

- Business sign-off documented (CSM) - success criteria met.
- Stability: 7 consecutive days with error rate < agreed threshold and latency within SLO at normal traffic.
- Knowledge transfer: runbook, escalation matrix, and key admin tasks documented with customer.
- QBR scheduled for 30 days post go-live.

Appendices

A. SLA summary (example)

| Item | SLA | Measurement | Credit/Action |
|------|-----|-------------|---------------|
| Uptime | 99.95% monthly | Synthetic checks + customer traffic | Credit per contract |
| P95 latency | Contract-specified | Observed on production route | Follow escalation for persistent breaches |

B. Contact matrix (example)

- CSM: marina.alvarez@redwood.ai | Phone: +1-555-0123
- Support L2: support-team@redwood.ai | PagerDuty: PD_SUPPORT
- Runtime on-call: runtime-oncall@redwood.ai | PagerDuty: PD_RUNTIME
